DOM from different sources and at a large concentration range enhanced the degradation of phenantherene, and the degradation rate was the highest when the DOM was from P.  elliottii litter and at 100mg/L.
the degradation of phenantrhene was enhanced by dissolved organic matter derived for different origins of forest leaf litter.

the effects of DOM on phenanthrene biodegradation and provides a new insight into the role of DOM in the remediation of PAHs.
the mechanism of how DOM derived from forest leaf litters promotes the degradation of phenantrene.
the effects of DOM on the degradation of PAHs in aqueous phase, which will help to better understand and manage the biodegradation of PAHs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DOM from different origins has a positive effect on the degradation of PAHs, but the mechanism is complex, and the effects are dependent on the composition of DOM.
the effects of DOM on phenanthrene degradation were the synergistic result of the stimulation of biological activity, the increase in phenanthrene bioavailabilty, and the co-metabolism of humic acid.
the effects of DOM on PAH biodegradation are complex and depend on the composition and concentration of DOM and on the characteristics of the PAH and the microorganism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DOM derived from leaf litter can be a promising alternative for the remediation of PAH-contaminated soil.

the DOM derived from Phe-1-degraded leaf litter is more efficient than the DOM derived from non-degraded leaf litter in enhancing phenanthrene degradation, and that DOM is more efficient than humic acid alone in enhancing phenanthrenes degradation.

the degradation of PAHs by Phe- 1 was promoted by DOM from leaf litter, which was due to the synergistic effects of the readily available nutrients in DOM, increased solubility and bioavailability of phenanthrene and co-metabolism of humic acid.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the degradation of PAHs in the aqueous phase can be enhanced by DOM released from forest leaf-litter.
DOM from forest leaf litter has a positive effect on phenanthrene degradation, which may be useful in bioremediation of PAHs.
the DOM released by the decomposition of leaf litter has a significant effect on phenanthrene degradation by Phe- 1.
